text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds run every time changes are made. This means the software is compiled and tested quickly and consistently. As part of the CI process, running tests helps check that new code works correctly and does not break existing features. One major benefit is catching issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results, into a clear sequence. This makes teamwork smoother and helps teams release reliable software more often.
